gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.approver: Devin (sole human, in chat with the producer)
gates.reason: Devin approved option A on 2026-09-15 from the B-roll Options page. No boot footage is shown; the words do that work. R14 rights position stands as documented.
gates.decision: Option A: use the acquired cutaway (Pexels 8888818) alone, 10 s from 00:00.500; narration carries 'booting'; frame or scale so the ViewSonic E70 wordmark is not prominent. Never label it a boot or caption 'Pentium'.

acquisition_evidence.approval: Devin approved this one download on 2026-09-15 (relayed by the B-roll Scouting Manager, session vb-bf). No other clip was downloaded; the Commons POST clip was not approved.
acquisition_evidence.access_barrier_encountered: None. HTTP 302 then 200. No login, payment, terms click-through, CAPTCHA or Cloudflare check appeared; nothing was bypassed.
acquisition_evidence.license_recorded: Pexels License (https://www.pexels.com/license/); attribution not required; credit optional as "Video by MART PRODUCTION from Pexels".
acquisition_evidence.ffprobe_verified: duration 11.8 s; 4096x2160; 25 fps; h264 High; video stream only, no audio stream. This matches the asset page's stated 4096x2160 / 25 fps / about 12 s. The 2732x1440 rendition seen during scouting was an in-page preview only.
acquisition_evidence.watermark_check: No watermark, baked-in caption or burned-in text in any inspected frame. Nothing was removed from the file; it is preserved byte-identical as downloaded.
acquisition_evidence.content_verified_at_full_resolution: Frames at 0.5 s, 5 s and 10.5 s viewed at native 4096x2160 and one frame at 720p. All three show a beige CRT monitor and keyboard on a desk in a dim room, with the CRT screen blank and dark throughout. There is no boot, no power-on, no POST, no memory count, no BIOS screen and no OS. No PC case or tower appears anywhere in frame.
acquisition_evidence.hardware_marking_now_legible: At full resolution the monitor bezel reads "ViewSonic" with the ViewSonic bird logo, plus an "E70" model marking on the upper-right bezel. This identifies a monitor make and model only. It is not a CPU, not a system identification and not a date, so it does not establish a Pentium-era machine and is not Pentium evidence. At 720p neither marking is legible.
acquisition_evidence.label_binding: This clip is a period-setting cutaway only. It must never be labelled a boot and must never be captioned with, or cut to imply, "Pentium".

gates.plan_assumption_checked: ASSET_PLAN.md:122 suggests 'YouTube clips (screenshot-able)'. That is not a rights basis: the standard YouTube license is not reuse permission, so YouTube leads are rights-blocked.
gates.shot_claim_checked: SCRIPT.md:805 'A Pentium-era PC booting up'. No free candidate shows a boot on a period PC, and no free candidate identifies a Pentium CPU. This is now confirmed against the acquired full-resolution file, not just previews: the acquired clip shows no boot and no CPU. Only the H02 LGR lead carries a creator-stated Pentium (100MHz), and that is unverified on screen.
